title: Why one huge value messes up the mean
examples: Why is the median better than the mean for pay?
How does an outlier affect the mean?

explain.say: Five people work at a small shop. Look at their yearly pay: 20, 25, 30 and 35 thousand dollars, and the boss gets 390 thousand. Look at that last bar!

draw.text: Why one huge value messes up the mean

explain.say: Let us find the mean. Add them up: 500 thousand. Share between 5 people: 100 thousand each. But wait. Does anyone except the boss earn anywhere near 100?
No! One huge value pulls the mean up. A value far away from the rest is called an outlier. Now find the median, the middle value. Look at Chidi's bar. What is it?
30 thousand. The median does not care how big the outlier is, so it shows typical pay much better. Look at the two bars. Which average would the boss like to tell everyone?

faq.a: An outlier is a value much bigger or much smaller than the rest of the data, like the boss's 390 thousand.

faq.q: Why does an outlier change the mean so much?
faq.a: The mean adds every value, so one huge number adds a lot to the total. Shared out, it lifts everyone's share.
asks: How does an outlier affect the mean?

faq.q: When should you use the median instead of the mean?
faq.a: Use the median when there are outliers or the data is lopsided, like pay or house prices. It shows the typical value better.

faq.q: Why do news reports use median pay?
faq.a: A few very high earners pull the mean up, so the median is closer to what an ordinary worker earns.

faq.q: What is the new median with six people?
faq.a: In order the pay is 20, 25, 30, 30, 35 and 390. The two middle values are 30 and 30, so the median is 30 thousand.

facts: The median is not affected by how extreme the largest or smallest value is.
Many governments report median household income because the mean is pulled up by very high incomes.

quiz.say: Find the mean and median of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 36.
quiz.why: The total is 50, shared by 5 gives 10. The middle value is 4.

wrong.1: This swaps the mean and the median.
wrong.2: The median is the middle value, 4, not the mean.

quiz.say: Which average is affected most by an outlier?
quiz.why: The mean adds up every value, so one extreme value changes it a lot.

wrong.1: The median only looks at the middle value.
wrong.2: The mode only looks at the most common value.
